answers.answer: Reveal a shuffled region card for the King; each player takes another region card as their home and places their Grande there. Their ten Caballeros go: two in home beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal top card for King; another card sets home; initial ten are 2 home, 1 track, 7 court.

answers.answer: In round 1 players choose the starter. Later, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts; others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: chosen starter; later prior last-turn player; clockwise; no value may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, before choosing an action card, recruit up to the allowance pictured on your power card from provinces into court; you may recruit fewer.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: descending value; recruit at start of turn; after recruitment choose action.

answers.answer: If provinces lack enough of your color, take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King's region cannot supply them, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3: may take own from board; King's region taboo; Castillo cannot supply outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment is from court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo. It may be divided among destinations. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: stacks allow up to their number; from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo, dividing allowance freely.

answers.answer: Yes, do deployment and the special action in either order. Each activity must be completed before the other begins; neither can be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 4: either order, complete one before other; may decline special action.

answers.answer: After your turn, set the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. After all turns, discard remaining face-up cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected laid aside; remaining discarded after turns; King card revealed again and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region; special actions do not override this. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment and protected locations: King's region taboo; may still be scored; actions moving King change protected region.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros enter the Castillo. King's location does not restrict entry. Caballeros leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: any or all may go into Castillo regardless of King's location; announce number; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: After rounds 3, 6, and 9: (1) secretly choose one destination per player's Castillo Caballeros before uncovering it, excluding the King's region; (2) uncover and score Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move all Castillo pieces to chosen regions, then replace empty Castillo; (4) score the nine regions in track order.
answers.evidence: General scoring: stages 1–4; destinations chosen before uncovering; Castillo scored, emptied, then regions scored.

answers.answer: A player's Castillo Caballeros must all go to one region, so they cannot be split or kept in Castillo. The King's region is prohibited. If illegally chosen, that player's pieces go to their court.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages 1 and 3: all pieces go to one region; King's region prohibited; illegal choice sends pieces to court; none retained.

answers.answer: The three players tied with four each score 3 points apiece; the player with three scores 1. Grandes do not count as Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Scoring example on 5/3/1 counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1; only Caballeros count.

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6; the player with 3 scores 4; each player with 2 scores 0. This is before bonuses.
answers.evidence: Scoring example on 6/4/2 counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: Two-player games pay only first place; three-player games pay first and second. In a two-player tie for first, each shifts to second, beyond the payable rank, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first; three first and second; two-player tie for first pays neither after rank shift.

answers.answer: Bonuses apply whenever the region is scored, including special scoring. The sole majority holder in the King's region gets +2; a sole majority holder with their own Grande in that region gets +2 home bonus. Neither applies on a first-place tie.
answers.evidence: Bonuses: +2 King's, +2 Home; apply whenever relevant region scored, including special scorings; neither on tie.

answers.answer: No. Special Castillo scoring uncovers and scores the contents, then covers the same pieces again; it does not redistribute or empty them.
answers.evidence: Special scoring Castillo: score contents then cover same Caballeros; redistribution waits for general scoring.

answers.answer: Yes, a mobile scoreboard may be placed at Castillo. It cannot move into or out of the King's region, cannot be stacked on the other, and must remain right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, not rotated.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King's region; cannot stack; never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region except the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. It becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: destination restrictions, cannot leave King's region, destination may contain several Grandes, becomes new home.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which, though taking the visible top card is apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: any one played card including this turn; need not reveal which.

answers.answer: The game ends after completing all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins.
answers.evidence: Overview and End: after third general scoring; furthest along success track wins.

answers.answer: Separate action cards by the 1–5 Caballero backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. Reveal the top card of each stack (five cards) each round. The standard marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup and Turn Structure: five stacks shuffled separately; reveal top of each; marker starts at 1.

answers.answer: No. Played power cards remain in each player's face-up used stack with only the top card visible; a special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: cards remain in face-up used stack, only top visible, rather than returning to hand.

answers.answer: Use the King's new position if you move him before deploying; the King card lets you place him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: if move King before deployment use new position; Stack 5: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: Place the Veto before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: retain to stop one special action; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: Yes, while Veto is held others must announce special actions before execution. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; executed parts are not undone.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: announce; object as soon as starts; incomplete remainder can be stopped; completed cannot; executed parts not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: discard after use; unused discard at end of next round.

answers.answer: Every fellow player except the selecting player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros; empty court sends none; selector unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player sends all two Caballeros they have to the provinces because they have fewer than three. Your five are unaffected because the selecting player is exempt.
answers.evidence: Decay — three from court: each fellow player sends three or all if fewer; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed paragraph and card face say each player, including the selector, sends three own Caballeros to provinces. Start with the player to selector's left, proceed clockwise, selector last. Each chooses from any regions and/or court, excluding King's region and Castillo. The heading instead says 'fellow players.' No explicit shortfall rule is supplied.
answers.evidence: The King returns: detailed paragraph/card say each player, three own, sources and order; heading says fellow players; no shortfall rule.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner's provinces. No court pieces, King's region, or Castillo. No fallback is specified for a player without an eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each: selecting player chooses; each player including selector; no courts, King's region, Castillo; no fallback.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk; choices are revealed together. It must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros, and two return to provinces. The King's region and Castillo are excluded as sources.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: choose simultaneously/reveal together; region must contain at least two; never King's region or Castillo. The requested fallback is unsupported if protected King's region causes ambiguity.

answers.answer: If the player has at most one in every region, choose a region containing one and return that one. This fallback is stated for the singleton-everywhere case. The action does not give a procedure for no eligible pieces.
answers.evidence: Secret removal of two: singleton fallback if at most one in every region; choose region with one and return that one.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects on their disk, then all reveal together. The chosen region must contain at least one of their Caballeros; return all their own there to provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected; King's region and Castillo are excluded.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous disk selection; at least one; return all; none anywhere is unaffected; no King's region/Castillo.

answers.answer: Yes, choose any region including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal scoring rules, rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is scored, cover the same pieces again; they are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Pick one region to score: any including King's region or Castillo; normal rules/bonuses; cover same Castillo pieces.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia, Catalonia, and Seville. Eligibility uses the current first value, so Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable home and King's bonuses apply.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions: printed group; current first value determines eligibility; mobile examples; special scorings follow normal scoring and bonuses.

answers.answer: Printed 5-value group: Basque Country, Aragon, Valencia. Printed 6/7 group: Old Castile, New Castile, Granada. Current first values, including mobile scoreboard replacements, determine category eligibility. Castillo is excluded from all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Special scoring table lists groups by current first value and says Castillo is not scored in all-5.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; a tie for first scores nothing, and lower ranks get nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First position only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Score all board regions tied for most Caballeros. Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more than either region.
answers.evidence: Most Caballeros: score all tied board regions; Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions, score all tied for least, and exclude empty regions and Castillo.
answers.evidence: Least Caballeros: compare nonempty regions; all ties score; empty regions and Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each secretly chooses another region with their disk and reveals simultaneously. Choosing the King's region or the region being vacated sends that player's group to their court. King's region pieces cannot be taken out; Castillo cannot be emptied with this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement: fellow players move all own; secret disk choices revealed together; King's/vacated choice sends pieces to court; taboo and Castillo limits.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, no more than one region away. The King card allows any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: neighboring region/no more than one; King card: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to court. This is separate from the card's ordinary up-to-four deployment from court to board; either activity can go first and each is completed as a whole.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four deployment; either order.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on disks and reveal simultaneously. A uniquely chosen region is scored under normal rules; if multiple players chose the same region, it is not scored. Disk includes nine board regions including King's region, not Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: simultaneous choices; unique scores; duplicates do not; disk includes King's region, not Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or Castillo; some may return to the original region. Origins exclude King's region and Castillo, and destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table: all-own effect allows return to original; general restrictions exclude King's region/Castillo origins and King's region destinations.

answers.answer: Up to two additional Caballeros from court via special action plus the normal up-to-one deployment, for up to three total. The additional two may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo; only normal deployment must be adjacent to the King.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two-more: up to two additional from court, total up to three; only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one special alternative, not both. The normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice card: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros, all from one origin region, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. They cannot come from multiple origins.
answers.evidence: Intrigue up to five: one origin, own and/or foreign, to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three other players' Caballeros from any non-King board regions, including multiple origins; none may come from Castillo, and your own pieces are not included. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any three foreign: up to three other players, multiple non-King origins, never Castillo as source; any non-King destinations/Castillo.

answers.answer: Any three allows up to three own and/or foreign from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. Any four allows up to four own and/or foreign from any non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Both are subject to the general source exclusions of King's region and Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table distinguishes any three/any four; general relocation origins exclude King's region/Castillo; destinations as specified.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros, separate ownership allowances, from any regions. Multiple origin regions are allowed. Relocation origins exclude King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo. The row does not specify more restrictive 'other regions' wording.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two-own-and-two-foreign: separate allowances; from any regions. General rules: origins exclude King's region/Castillo; destinations exclude King's region, may include Castillo. Exact destination relative to every selected origin is not specified.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, your own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo is excluded as an origin; destinations may include it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any four of your own: up to four own only; non-King origins; other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: For each-player secret scoring, a player may choose the King's region but not Castillo; choices are simultaneous and duplicates do not score. The separate pick-one-region action allows its player to choose either King's region or Castillo and scores normally; Castillo pieces remain covered and are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring disk includes King's region, not Castillo; Stack 2 pick-one allows King's region or Castillo and covers Castillo pieces again.

answers.answer: Both mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The special action may introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup: place both beside board. Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: introduce from beside board or move one already on it.
